## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: Osaka Metropolitan University (OMU) online classes after the October 2026 outage (compiled 2026-10-05)

## 1. What the resolution sources say now
- **@OsakaMetUniv on X:** we could not read it. x.com returned 403 on 2026-10-05, so we have no direct quote from the account.
- **OMU main website:** www.omu.ac.jp refused connections on 2026-10-05.
- **OMU's interim outage page** (https://e.omu.ac.jp/announce/1.html and https://e.omu.ac.jp/announce/?p=16):
  - It says the core systems, campus systems and network are unavailable: 「基盤システム、各種学内システム、ネットワークが利用できない状態」.
  - When last read, it said the cause was under investigation and that updates would go on the "OMU entrance" page.
  - It gives no date for online classes.
  - The page seems to date from 2–3 Oct, so it may now be out of date.
- **Unverified:** a blog (https://kkm-mako.com/blog/articles/omu-system-outage-unipa/) mentions a temporary notice site at www.omu.moe. We have not confirmed it is official.
- **Key wording on online classes (as of 2026-10-05):**
  - The university says the restart date for online classes will be decided based on how system recovery goes: 「オンライン授業については、システムの復旧状況を踏まえて再開時期を判断します」.
  - Source: セキュリティ対策Lab, 2026-10-05, https://rocket-boys.co.jp/security-measures-lab/osaka-metropolitan-university-ransomware-update-20261005/
  - MBS on 2026-10-05 reported the same position: https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/4d139d586213ccab1bea8ea57e005e6689c4ab6b
  - **Uncertain:** the exact Japanese wording came through a tool that summarises pages, and we could not check it against the original.
- **How close to resolving:** online classes are suspended with no date set. There is no recovery forecast either: 「復旧のめどは立っていません」 (NHK and Kansai TV, 2026-10-05).

## 2. Timeline and current situation
- **2026-10-02, about 00:30 JST:** the core infrastructure, campus systems and network failed. It was the last day for course-registration corrections.
  - At 11:00, 10 of 13 main system components were unreachable.
  - All classes were cancelled that day on all five campuses (森之宮, 杉本, 中百舌鳥, 阿倍野, りんくう).
  - Source: ITmedia, 2026-10-02, https://www.itmedia.co.jp/news/article/2610/02/2000001953/
- **2026-10-02, evening:** cancellation extended to all faculties for 2–8 October, with in-person classes scheduled to restart from 9 October.
  - Source: Yomiuri TV via Yahoo, 2026-10-02, https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/991fc60aa0878dba588515a9ace42c1a7abecc1f
  - NHK also reported it: https://news.web.nhk/newsweb/na/nb-2000105970
- **2026-10-05:** at a press conference the university confirmed a ransomware attack.
  - President 櫻木弘之 apologised, and the police have been consulted.
  - **Uncertain date:** one search snippet put the conference on 4 October.
  - Sources:
    - Kansai TV: https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/dfc089162d28c04cbdba6b4d830c5142ea41d4b1
    - livedoor: https://news.livedoor.com/topics/detail/32493125/
    - Nikkei: https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUF057NR0V01C26A0000000/
- **Damage (reported 2026-10-05):**
  - The attack hit the virtualisation platform, and about 500 servers are down.
  - Most backups were also encrypted.
  - Personal data of at least 130,000 people is on the affected systems; whether it leaked is under investigation.
  - The university hospital's medical-record systems were not affected.
  - ABC reports signs of data tampering and says the prefectural police plan to investigate: https://news.infoseek.co.jp/article/abcnews_62882/
- **Systems down (ITmedia, 2026-10-02):**
  - the campus network
  - the UNIPA student portal
  - Moodle, the learning system used for course materials and assignments
  - the OMU+ app
  - OMU email
  - the course catalogue
  - staff systems
  - the website
- **Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace:** no source says whether they are affected.
  - Students were told to use personal email addresses for scholarship applications, which suggests their OMU accounts are not usable.
  - **Uncertain:** OMU email may run on Microsoft 365. This is an inference only.
- **In-person classes from 9 October:** they are to run on a backup network with alternative ways of sharing data (ABC). The plan is still described as scheduled (予定), not certain.

**Events scheduled before 15 October:**
- **2–8 October:** all classes cancelled.
- **9 October (Friday):** in-person classes planned to restart.
- **Course registration:** corrections and the second-round lottery for general-education courses are postponed, with no new dates published.
- **Admissions:** the application deadline for comprehensive-selection (総合型選抜) admissions is extended to 22 October at 17:00 (rocket-boys and kkm-mako).
- **Not found:** any scheduled date for announcing online classes.

**Prediction markets:** we did not find any market on this question.

## 3. Base rates: how long recovery took after similar attacks
- **In-person classes after university ransomware attacks** usually return within about 1–7 days. Examples: Howard University 2021 (about 5 days) and University of Hertfordshire 2021 (about 5 days, secondary source only).
- **Online systems where the university's own servers were encrypted:**

| Institution | Incident | What came back, and when | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reitaku University | Ransomware, 2024-08-27, during summer break | Moodle 2024-09-10 (14 days); everything 2024-09-27 | https://cite.reitaku-u.ac.jp/news/2024-08-30/1209 |
| Tokai University | Ransomware, 2025-04-16 | LMS, portal and email back to normal 2025-07-16 (about 3 months) | https://www.u-tokai.ac.jp/news-notice/1352134/ |
| University of Duisburg-Essen | Ransomware, November 2022 | Learning platforms usable on campus only after about 10 days; wider services about 5–6 weeks | https://lokalklick.eu/2022/12/07/ude-nach-schwerem-cyberangriff-wiederherstellung-digitaler-systeme-laeuft-auf-hochtouren/ |
| Howard University | Ransomware, September 2021 | In-person classes after about 5 days; online/hybrid undergraduate classes after about 2–3 weeks (date uncertain); graduate courses continued on Zoom and Teams throughout | https://thewash.org/2021/09/28/howard-university-continues-to-investigate-ransomware-attack-as-classes-resume/ |
| Lincoln College (US) | Ransomware, December 2021 | About 3 months; the college then closed | https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2022/05/college-closes-down-after-ransomware-attack |
| Osaka General Medical Center (hospital, not a university) | Ransomware, 2022-10-31 | Core systems after 43 days; fully normal after 73 days | https://xtech.nikkei.com/atcl/nxt/column/18/01157/012600079/ |
| Canvas (cloud learning system, vendor-side incident) | May 2026 | Back within about 1–6 days | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Canvas_data_breach |

- **Where OMU sits:** with about 500 servers, the virtualisation platform hit and backups encrypted, it is at the severe end of these cases.
- **Possible faster route:** a university can announce that online classes are back using unaffected cloud tools such as Teams, Zoom or Google before its learning system is restored, as Howard's graduate courses did. Whether OMU has such tools available is **unknown**.

## Notes on what counts
- Everything above happened after the 2 October 2026 outage, which the question is built around.
- The restart of in-person classes on 9 October does not count toward YES.
- A restart in only some departments does not count either; the university has to announce it generally.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, as of 23:59 Japan Standard Time (JST) on October 15, 2026, Osaka Metropolitan University (OMU) has officially announced that online (remote) classes have resumed — i.e., that the restriction suspending online/remote classes imposed after the October 2, 2026 information-systems outage has been lifted for the university generally. It resolves NO if no such resumption has been announced, or if online classes remain suspended/undecided, as of that time. Resolution is based on official OMU announcements, including posts on the university's official X account (https://x.com/OsakaMetUniv) and the OMU website/entrance page, or reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). An announcement dated, for example, October 14, 2026 stating that remote classes resume October 15 counts as YES.
letra_pequena: The resumption of in-person (face-to-face) classes, which the university planned to restart from October 9, 2026, does NOT by itself count toward YES; the question concerns the resumption of online/remote classes specifically. If OMU resumes online classes for some faculties or graduate schools but not others, the question resolves YES only if the university has issued a general announcement that online/remote classes have resumed (not merely for an isolated department). If OMU's website remains inaccessible, the official X account (@OsakaMetUniv) and credible news reporting serve as the resolution source. If no credible information on the status of online classes can be located, the question resolves NO.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About ten days, until 23:59 JST on October 15.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. Online classes remain suspended, with no restart date announced.

(c) **Reference class:** Recovery of online teaching after university ransomware attacks has ranged from roughly two weeks to several months. In the small set of comparable cases provided, a university-wide restart within 13 days of the outage looks uncommon; OMU’s reported damage to servers and backups makes rapid recovery less likely.

(d) **NO scenario:** In-person classes restart on October 9, but the systems needed for remote teaching remain unavailable, so OMU does not lift the online-class suspension by October 15.

(e) **YES scenario:** OMU restores sufficient teaching services—or establishes an alternative platform—and announces a general restart of online classes by the deadline.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** Working systems alone do not suffice: the criteria require an **official general announcement** that online classes have resumed. An in-person restart or an isolated department’s online restart does not count.

Probability: 24%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days, until 23:59 JST on October 15.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. Online classes remain suspended, with no resumption date announced.

(c) **Reference class:** After major university ransomware outages, teaching can restart in person before the systems needed for online classes recover. The examples provided range from roughly two weeks to months for online learning systems; OMU’s reported damage to servers and backups points toward the slower end.

(d) **NO scenario:** OMU resumes face-to-face teaching on October 9, but its learning systems remain unavailable and it has not generally lifted the online-class suspension by October 15.

(e) **YES scenario:** OMU restores enough systems—or adopts workable alternative tools—and officially announces a general resumption of remote classes by the deadline.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** In-person classes or a restart in isolated departments do not count. An official announcement by the deadline that online classes resume *on* October 15 does count.

Probability: 20%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days, from 2026-10-05 to 23:59 JST on 2026-10-15.

(b) **Status quo:** Online classes are suspended, no resumption date has been set, and there is no recovery outlook (「復旧のめどは立っていません」). If nothing changes, the question resolves NO.

(c) **Reference class:** University ransomware incidents in which the institution's own servers, the virtualisation layer and the backups were encrypted.
- Restoring the learning system (LMS) usually takes 2 weeks to 3 months:
  - Reitaku: Moodle back after 14 days, during a break.
  - Duisburg-Essen: about 10 days, on campus only.
  - Tokai: about 3 months.
  - Howard: online undergraduate classes back after about 2–3 weeks.
- OMU is at the severe end: about 500 servers down, the virtualisation platform hit, most backups encrypted, and data tampering under police investigation.
- Base rate of a general online-class resumption within 13 days for an incident this severe: roughly 15–25%.

(d) **NO scenario:** In-person classes restart on 9 October on the backup network. Moodle, UNIPA and the OMU accounts stay down while forensics and a rebuild continue. The university keeps saying online classes will restart "depending on recovery," or quietly moves some courses to in-person. No general announcement comes by 15 October.

(e) **YES scenario:** Student identities are managed in the cloud (Microsoft 365 or Google), and those services are not affected. Under pressure to restore teaching, the university announces around 12–14 October that online classes resume using Teams or Zoom, with materials shared through alternative means, even though Moodle is not yet restored.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- YES requires a general official announcement that online or remote classes have resumed. A resumption by one department, or online courses being converted to in-person, does not count.
- An announcement dated on or before 15 October that names a future resumption date may be ambiguous. The stated example only covers a resumption date of 15 October itself.
- If no credible information can be found, the question resolves NO.
- Japanese universities tend to be cautious after ransomware, especially when backups are compromised and account credentials may be exposed. That makes a quick reopening of remote access less likely.

Probability: 18%
